scenes.text: VGGT stacks 24 pairs of different transformer blocks. What if one pair, run again and again, did the same job?
scenes.say: VGGT stacks twenty-four pairs of different blocks to rebuild a scene from photos. What if one pair, run again and again, did the same job?

scenes.headline: How one looped block turns photos into 3D
scenes.sub: Déjà View, from NVIDIA: cameras and depth from one shared block
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Oswin! Déjà View rebuilds a scene by running the same block over and over. Let's open it up.

scenes.title: Photos in, geometry out
scenes.sub: What a feed-forward reconstructor has to produce
scenes.say: Chapter one. Photos in, geometry out.

scenes.title: The usual way: a deep stack

steps.say: Hand the model photos from different angles. An encoder turns each one into patch tokens.

steps.term: Global attention: every token sees every view
steps.say: VGGT pushes them through twenty-four pairs of different blocks. Frame attention looks within one photo; global attention looks across all of them.
Heads read out depth maps, point maps and cameras.
Accuracy grew with size: VGGT has one point two six billion parameters.

scenes.credit: video from NVIDIA's post on X

steps.say: Here is the job, from NVIDIA's post. Drone footage goes in; a point cloud and the camera's path come out.

scenes.title: One block, sixteen times
scenes.say: Chapter two. One block, sixteen times.

scenes.text: Make the refinement explicit: one shared block of frame and global attention, applied K times to the same tokens.
scenes.say: Deep stacks seem to refine their answer layer by layer. So make that explicit: one shared block, applied K times to the same tokens.

steps.say: The paper's diagram. Encoder tokens on the left, two shallow decoders on the right.
In the middle, one block, frame then global attention, fed back into itself K times.

labels: the state starts as DINOv2 features

steps.term: State: the tokens the loop keeps refining
steps.say: Each loop reads the whole state, every token of every view, and writes a refined one.
Decode it after two loops: the room is smeared, the cameras far off.
After four, the walls start to line up.
After eight, the cameras are close.
After sixteen, sharp geometry and accurate cameras. Training only ever checks the last step.

scenes.say: Inside, an ordinary block with three dials.

parts.say: Attention, then an MLP, each added with a scale per channel.

parts.note: the scales come from the step's time
parts.say: The scales come from a tiny network that reads where this step starts and ends in time. That is how one block tells an early step from a late one.

parts.note: the state gate, below 1 on average
parts.say: Then a state gate scales everything. In the released weights it sits below one, so older content fades.

steps.say: I counted the checkpoint's tensors. Three quarters is the encoder, eighty-six point six million, run once per photo.
The block doing the multi-view reasoning is fourteen and a half million, run sixteen times.
Two shallow decoders read out depth and rays.
One hundred and seventeen million in all. Untied, sixteen copies would make it about three hundred and twenty-nine million.

scenes.title: Turning the dial
scenes.sub: One checkpoint, any K from 8 to 16

scenes.title: Training for any loop count
scenes.say: One checkpoint serves every loop count from eight to sixteen.

items.say: Each batch draws a loop count between eight and sixteen, favouring the high end.
The gates read time, not a step number, so one set of weights fits every count.
Only the final state is scored.

scenes.title: Fewer loops: re-grid, don't stop early

steps.say: Want fewer loops? You could stop the sixteen-step schedule early.
Or run K steps on a K-step time grid. That wins at every budget.
At eight loops, pose AUC at three degrees is zero point four three, against zero point three one for stopping early.

scenes.title: Forward TFLOPs at 24 views
scenes.say: Now the bill. Ten times fewer parameters is not ten times fewer FLOPs: half or less of Pi3 and VGGT, about the same as Depth Anything 3 Large.

scenes.title: Where one loop's FLOPs go, 24 views

steps.say: Why so close? Count one loop. The linear layers cost under one teraflop.
Frame attention is cheap: each photo sees only its own tokens.
Global attention is three of the four teraflops, every token looking at all thirty-one thousand. Sharing weights does not touch that.

scenes.title: Does it hold up?
scenes.sub: Benchmarks, and where the dial breaks
scenes.say: Chapter four. Does it hold up?

steps.say: A sign the loop does real work: one patch's global attention onto another view, loop by loop.
It starts diffuse and settles on the matching point, though training never asked for matches.
And the limit. Past sixteen loops the state drifts; past about thirty steps, it collapses.

scenes.title: Where it stops
scenes.say: What I found checking the claims.

items.text: Best on average, rarely per cell
items.say: It leads the averages, an inlier ratio of eighty point three, but wins few single cells against the concurrent VGGT Omega.
Shared beat untied blocks, but only in half-length runs.
And the quick-start script runs twelve loops; the tables use sixteen.

scenes.text: Tying weights shrinks parameters, not FLOPs. The loop count is a real dial for precise camera poses.
scenes.say: Tying weights shrinks parameters, not FLOPs. And the loop count is a real dial, above all for precise camera poses.

recap: Fewer loops: re-grid, don't stop early
scenes.say: To recap. One shared block, looped. Most parameters are the encoder. For fewer loops, re-grid; don't stop early.
